_comment: Tracks IETF/OpenID drafts implemented in this PoC. Updated daily by the standards-tracker GitHub Actions workflow. Set implemented_rev when the PoC code is updated to match a new revision.

wg_feeds.name: IETF WIMSE WG
wg_feeds.note: Discovers new WIMSE WG drafts not yet in our baseline

wg_feeds.name: IETF OAuth WG
wg_feeds.note: Discovers new OAuth WG drafts (DPoP updates, Transaction Tokens, etc.)

wg_feeds.name: OpenID Foundation
wg_feeds.note: Catches OIDF spec publications, errata, and public review periods

standards.label: WIMSE Workload Identity Credentials (WIT / AgentToken base)
standards.impact: AgentToken (agent+jwt) extends WIT structure — any cnf.jwk or typ changes affect pkg/identity

standards.label: WIMSE Workload Proof Token (AgentProofToken base)
standards.impact: AgentProofToken (application/agent-proof+jwt) mirrors WPT claims — aud, wth, tth (Txn-Token hash), jti

standards.label: WIMSE Workload Identifier
standards.impact: SPIFFE URI format for agent SVIDs — spiffe://trust-domain/path

standards.label: WIMSE Mutual TLS Binding
standards.impact: Token-cert binding in gateway middleware — URI SAN matching against AgentToken.sub

standards.label: WIMSE Architecture
standards.impact: Token exchange, trust domain boundaries, delegation chain semantics

standards.label: Credential Broker for Agents (CB4A)
standards.impact: TRE JWT (tre+jwt), PDP decision (pdp-decision+jwt), CB4A token (cb4a-token+jwt), Tier model, DPoP binding via cnf.jkt

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Transaction Tokens (Txn-Token)
standards.impact: Txn-Token (txntoken+jwt) propagates user identity + authorization context through agent chains; tth in AgentProofToken links proof to transaction; req_wl carries requesting agent SPIFFE ID

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 DPoP (RFC 9449)
standards.impact: DPoP proof JWT (dpop+jwt), cnf.jkt thumbprint, ath binding, jti replay protection in CDP

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693)
standards.impact: act claim (§4.1) in Txn-Token and JWT Authorization Grant — act.sub carries the entry-point agent SPIFFE ID acting on behalf of the user (sub); nested act represents prior actors in multi-hop chains. may_act (§4.4) reserved for future explicit delegation grants.

standards.label: OpenID Federation 1.0
standards.impact: Entity Configuration, Subordinate Statement, authority_hints, chain resolution for cross-org AgentToken validation

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 SPIFFE Client Authentication
standards.impact: AgentToken used as JWT bearer client assertion to authenticate to OAuth AS — eliminates shared secrets for agent-to-OAuth-AS authentication; WIT-SVID profile directly uses AgentToken

standards.label: OAuth Identity and Authorization Chaining Across Domains
standards.impact: JWT authorization grant (RFC 7523 profile) for cross-domain token exchange (RFC 8693); AS-A validates AgentToken and issues grant targeting AS-B; AS-B validates grant and issues its own access token; complements Txn-Token for multi-trust-domain agent chains

standards.label: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
standards.impact: Compliance audit applied 2026-08-02: all validators now enforce WithValidMethods (ES256), WithExpirationRequired, WithIssuedAt, and typ header checks. Key confusion, alg:none, and missing-exp attacks are mitigated across all packages.

standards.label: WIMSE Workload-to-Workload Authentication with HTTP Signatures
standards.impact: Alternative to AgentProofToken (JWT-based) for workload-to-workload proof — uses RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures. Tracked for future variant of pkg/identity/proof.go if WG adopts as primary mechanism.

standards.label: WIMSE Workload Identity Practices
standards.impact: Best practices for securing AI agent workload credentials: short-lived creds, no long-lived agent secrets, cert rotation. Mirrors AgentToken short-TTL design and CB4A vault-backed no-secret-at-rest model. Note: draft explicitly excludes WIMSE architecture specs — monitor for any AI-agent-specific guidance added.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: monitored. Best practices doc, not a protocol spec. Primary home is wimse-identity-fabric (general workload identity patterns). Here: relevant insofar as CB4A and AgentToken implement the 'no long-lived secrets' best practice.

standards.label: AuthZEN Binding for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
standards.impact: HIGH — directly covers the agent token exchange flows this PoC implements: identity chaining, ID-JAG grants, and Txn-Token issuance. Externalises the AS policy decision (which agent may exchange which token for which audience) to an AuthZEN PDP API. Our InMemoryPDP in internal/authz is a simplified stand-in for the AuthZEN five-tuple evaluation model. Rev 00 — monitor for when the WG adopts; implementation would connect CB4A PDP to a standard AuthZEN API.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: monitored. Rev 00, very early. High relevance to AI agent identity chaining and Txn-Token issuance flows. Callout added in CB4A demo tab.

standards.label: AuthZEN Profile for OAuth 2.0 Token Issuance
standards.impact: Parent spec for AuthZEN-TE. Defines the five-tuple (subject, resource, action, context, environment) for externalising OAuth token issuance decisions to a PDP via the AuthZEN Authorization API. Companion to draft-gazitt-oauth-authzen-token-exchange. Rev 00 — monitor.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: monitored. Companion to authzen-token-exchange. Defines the canonical PDP evaluation API that our InMemoryPDP loosely follows.

standards.label: Credential Delegation Protocol for AI Agents in Multi-System Environments
standards.impact: Competing/complementary approach to CB4A for agent credential delegation. Introduces typed delegation tokens that may differ from CB4A's TRE+PDP+CDP model. Noted in Credential Broker demo tab.

standards.label: Cross-Organizational Delegation for Workload and Agent Identity
standards.impact: Formalises cross-org delegation requirements — informs Identity Chaining scenario (pkg/identitychaining) and AgentChain semantics. Noted in Identity Chaining demo tab.

standards.label: Identity Propagation Context for Multi-Hop Delegation in OAuth 2.0 Environments
standards.impact: Multi-hop identity propagation context travelling with delegation chains — augments Identity Chaining and Txn-Token scenarios. Noted in Identity Chaining demo tab.

standards.label: Credential Delegation Protocol for AI Agents in Multi-System Environments
standards.impact: Formalises credential delegation semantics for AI agents across WIMSE trust domains — directly adjacent to AgentChain (pkg/identity/chain.go) and cross-domain delegation. Monitor for WG adoption; if adopted would formalize patterns already implemented in pkg/identity and internal/gateway.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Individual draft, highest relevance of new discoveries, no implementation change needed yet.

standards.label: SD-JWT-based Verifiable Digital Credentials (SD-JWT VC)
standards.impact: SD-JWT VC is for human-facing credential presentation. CB4A credentials use custom JWT types (cb4a-token+jwt, pdp-decision+jwt) — intentionally NOT SD-JWT VC format. Distinction: SD-JWT VC targets verifiable credentials for humans; CB4A targets per-request M2M governance tokens.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Tracked but not implemented; CB4A uses distinct token types.

standards.label: OAuth Proof of Possession Tokens with HTTP Message Signatures
standards.impact: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures as OAuth PoP mechanism — same design space as AgentProofToken per-request proof but using HTTP Signatures rather than a separate JWT. Monitor: if WG adopts this direction it could affect the long-term role of AgentProofToken.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Adjacent to AgentProofToken design space, monitor only.

standards.label: JWT Profile for OAuth 2.0 Enveloped Proof of Possession (EPOP)
standards.impact: Enveloped PoP embeds proof inside the token rather than a separate JWT (DPoP/AgentProofToken pattern). Adjacent to AgentProofToken and CB4A DPoP proof; monitor for convergence with existing PoP mechanisms.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Adjacent to AgentProofToken/DPoP design space, monitor only.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Delegated Authorization
standards.impact: OAuth delegated authorization patterns — could inform AgentChain delegation semantics and cross-domain identity chaining (pkg/identitychaining). Monitor for M2M delegation relevance.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Low-medium relevance, monitor only.

standards.label: Delegated Refresh Tokens for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
standards.impact: Async delegated refresh tokens extending RFC 8693 token exchange. Tangentially relevant to cross-domain token exchange scenarios. Monitor only.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Low relevance, monitor only.

standards.label: Cross-Device Flows: Security Best Current Practice
standards.impact: Human cross-device authentication flows (TV/IoT login). Not applicable — PoC focuses on M2M agent identity, not human-facing authentication.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Dismissed — not relevant to M2M agent identity.

standards.label: CIBA Binding for OAuth Push-Based Authentication Device Discovery
standards.impact: Client Initiated Backchannel Authentication (CIBA) for human authentication via decoupled device. Not applicable — human-facing flow.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Dismissed — not relevant to M2M agent identity.

standards.label: Discovery and Device Lifecycle for OAuth Push-Based Authentication
standards.impact: Device lifecycle for CIBA push-based human authentication. Not applicable — human-facing flow.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Dismissed — not relevant to M2M agent identity.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Refresh Token Scope
standards.impact: Refresh token scope response for human OAuth clients. Not applicable — agent identity uses short-lived token re-issuance, not refresh token flows.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #10. Dismissed — not relevant to M2M agent identity.

standards.label: Identity Continuation Assertion for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
standards.impact: Defines an Identity Continuation Assertion (typ: oauth-identity-continuation+jwt, claims: identity_continuation_handle, act, cnf.jkt, jti, exp ≤300s) for preserving user identity context across service boundaries using RFC 8693 Token Exchange. Focuses on pairwise user subject identifiers propagated across IdP trust boundaries — different problem space from agent/workload identity (SPIFFE). Adjacent to pkg/identitychaining (jwt-authz-grant) and AgentChain delegation patterns; monitor for convergence.
standards._triage: 2026-08-05: assessed in issue #13. Agent-fabric uses SPIFFE workload identity (not pairwise user subjects), so the continuation handle mechanism does not apply directly. Monitor for convergence with identity chaining patterns.

standards.label: AAuth Protocol (Agentic Authorization)
standards.impact: AI-agent-specific authorization protocol — defines how agents request delegated permissions (scopes) for sub-tasks, with explicit user/operator approval flows. Directly addresses the gap in scene-landscape: OAuth+RFC 8693 does not define how an agent communicates the scope of what it needs to do, or how a user approves fine-grained agent actions. AAuth fills this with an agent-to-AS authorization request flow. When adopted, adds an AAuth request type alongside AgentToken and CB4A in the Auth Landscape tab.
